text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Each time code is added, automated builds start immediately. The CI pipeline then runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This process helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. Because problems are found quickly, they are easier and cheaper to fix. CI pipelines can also include steps like code quality checks and deployment. Overall, Continuous Integration helps teams work faster and more safely, and it leads to better software for users.
